summary: Iteration 24 — Full end-to-end testing of the new DRIVER MOBILE APP (PWA at /driver). Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_driver_app.py (17 tests) covering access-code issuance + regeneration, driver login (success + invalid + missing code), /driver/me, /driver/vehicle, /driver/vehicles, /driver/upload, /driver/walkaround, /driver/defect and cross-role security. 16/17 pytest passed. One CRITICAL security failure discovered: a DRIVER JWT can be used against MANAGER endpoints (GET /api/vehicles returned 200 with driver token). Frontend: PWA verified on mobile viewport (420x860). Invalid code correctly stays on login. Valid code logs into driver-home with 'Welcome back John Smith', reg 'AB12 CDE' and all 5 tiles. Walkaround screen renders exactly 24 checklist items grouped Internal/External; marking item 0 fail + note + Submit returns to home. Defect screen: severity=major + description + Submit works. Compliance shows 3 items (Licence/CPC/Tacho) with status chips + documents section. Vehicle screen shows reg + MOT/Service/Tax rows. Tacho screen renders upload UI. Manager side verified: Drivers page shows the 6-char code in the driver-access-code block and driver-code-value; edit dialog exposes the drv-assigned-vehicle Select. Maintenance > Daily Checks tab shows the driver's TEST walkaround with 'Defects found' badge. Maintenance > Defects tab shows the driver's defect 'TEST driver mobile defect - brake noise' with 'Reported by John Smith'.

critical.issue: CRITICAL AUTH BYPASS — a driver JWT is accepted as a manager token. `_authenticate()` in server.py decodes any JWT signed with JWT_SECRET and looks up `payload['user_id']`. Driver JWTs (create_driver_jwt) embed the operator's user_id under the same key AND set role='driver', but `_authenticate` never checks the role claim. Effect: any authenticated driver can call every manager endpoint (vehicles/drivers/defects/documents/operator/etc.) with their operator's full permissions, and can therefore read/mutate ALL fleet data, generate new access codes for other drivers, delete records, etc. Verified: GET /api/vehicles with Bearer <driver_token> returned 200 with the operator's full vehicle list. Fix: reject the JWT in _authenticate() when payload.get('role') == 'driver' (or require role in {None, 'manager', 'user'}).

minor.issue: Backend matches access_code exactly (case-sensitive) but the frontend upper-cases before submit. Codes are always stored upper-case (from _CODE_CHARS), so a lower-case code from other clients (curl/mobile paste) returns 401. Recommend either uppercasing the incoming code in driver_login or matching case-insensitively.
Returns a bare list of registration strings, not vehicle objects. Fine for internal use but non-obvious from the name; add OpenAPI response model or rename for clarity.

action_items: URGENT: In server.py `_authenticate()`, reject bearer tokens whose decoded payload has role=='driver' (or explicitly require the manager path). This is a full auth-bypass — a driver can currently impersonate their operator on every manager endpoint.
Consider making driver access-code lookup case-insensitive (upper() the input in POST /api/driver/login) since manager might read the code aloud in mixed case.
Optional: return vehicle objects (or at least {registration, id}) from GET /api/driver/vehicles for future UI use.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py `_authenticate` (lines 685-710) only checks JWT signature + user_id; it does not inspect the `role` claim, so a driver JWT which contains role='driver' but also user_id=<operator_id> passes as the operator. This is the root cause of the auth-bypass. `get_current_driver` correctly checks role='driver', but the reverse guard on the manager path is missing.

DriverApp.js is a single 400-line file with 6 sub-components (Login, Home, Walkaround, Defect, Compliance, Vehicle, Tacho). Readable but nearing the split threshold — consider extracting each screen into pages/driver/screens/*.js as it grows.

server.py `/api/driver/walkaround` and `/api/driver/defect` correctly force user_id, driver_id/driver_name and vehicle_reg server-side, ignoring any values the driver client sends. Good tenancy isolation ✓

Driver token has 30-day expiry — reasonable for a driver's on-vehicle device, but consider adding a manager-side 'revoke code' action already exposed as DELETE /api/drivers/{did}/access-code plus a JWT jti/version check if you want immediate revocation (currently only new codes are blocked; already-issued JWTs remain valid until expiry).
driverApi.js — no 401 interceptor to auto-logout the driver when the token expires; the user will just see empty screens.

fileUrl() in DriverApp.js embeds the driver token in a query string on <a href>. This works but the token now appears in browser history and any downstream referer headers. Acceptable trade-off (backend accepts ?auth=), but note for security posture.

rca of the issue: Auth-bypass RCA — Repro: (1) manager login → POST /api/drivers/{id}/access-code → get code; (2) POST /api/driver/login {code} → get driver_token; (3) GET /api/vehicles with `Authorization: Bearer <driver_token>` → expected 401/403, actual 200 with full vehicle list. Root cause: server.py `_authenticate()` decodes any HS256 JWT and reads payload['user_id'] to load a user document; driver JWTs happen to store the operator's user_id under that exact key so the same lookup succeeds and returns User(**operator_doc). The `role='driver'` claim is inspected only by get_current_driver, never by _authenticate/get_current_user. Mitigation: in _authenticate, immediately return None (or raise) if payload.get('role') == 'driver'. After the fix, pytest TestSecurity.test_driver_token_rejected_on_manager_endpoint will pass.
